text: The analysis identifies 5,526 costly+dispensable genes and interprets their composition as predominantly mobile genetic elements.
quote: The 5,526 costly+dispensable genes are overwhelmingly associated with mobile genetic elements.
heading: Costly+Dispensable Genes Are Mobile Genetic Elements

text: Costly+dispensable genes are enriched for mobile-element description keywords (OR=7.45, p=4.6e-71).
quote: They are **7.45x more likely** to contain mobile element keywords in their descriptions (transposase, integrase, phage, IS element, recombinase, prophage; OR=7.45, p=4.6e-71).
heading: Costly+Dispensable Genes Are Mobile Genetic Elements

text: Compared with costly+conserved genes, costly+dispensable genes show 11.7x enrichment of the mobile-element SEED category and 26.7x enrichment of Virulence, the latter based on 21 vs 4 genes.
quote: SEED functional enrichment confirms this: the "Phages, Prophages, Transposable elements, Plasmids" category is 11.7x enriched (FDR=1.3e-17) and "Virulence" is 26.7x enriched (FDR=5.6e-14, though based on small counts: 21 vs 4 genes) in costly+dispensable vs costly+conserved genes.
heading: Costly+Dispensable Genes Are Mobile Genetic Elements

text: Figure fig_seed_enrichment.png shows SEED top-level category enrichment by costly+dispensable versus costly+conserved status.
quote: ![SEED top-level category enrichment in costly+dispensable vs costly+conserved](figures/fig_seed_enrichment.png)
heading: Costly+Dispensable Genes Are Mobile Genetic Elements

text: Costly+dispensable genes have lower SEED and KEGG annotation rates than costly+conserved genes.
quote: - **Poorly annotated**: 50.8% have SEED annotations vs 74.9% for costly+conserved; only 20.0% have KEGG annotations vs 42.7%
heading: They Are Poorly Characterized Recent Acquisitions

text: Orphan genes account for 44.5% of costly+dispensable versus 13.1% of costly+conserved genes.
quote: - **Taxonomically restricted**: 44.5% are orphan genes (no ortholog group) vs 13.1% for costly+conserved
heading: They Are Poorly Characterized Recent Acquisitions

text: Median ortholog-group breadth is 15 organisms for costly+dispensable genes versus 31 for costly+conserved genes.
quote: - **Narrow ortholog breadth**: Median 15 organisms share the OG vs 31 for costly+conserved (Mann-Whitney p=4.0e-99, rank-biserial r=0.233)
heading: They Are Poorly Characterized Recent Acquisitions

text: 24.2% of costly+dispensable genes are singletons, whereas no costly+conserved genes are singletons.
quote: - **High singleton fraction**: 24.2% are singletons (found in only 1 genome); no costly+conserved genes are singletons.
heading: They Are Poorly Characterized Recent Acquisitions

text: The singleton contrast is partly structural because core genes cannot be singletons by definition.
quote: Note: this is partly structural since core genes cannot be singletons by definition.
heading: They Are Poorly Characterized Recent Acquisitions

text: Within dispensable genes, singleton enrichment among costly versus neutral genes is slight (OR=1.09, p=0.02).
quote: Within the dispensable category, costly genes are only slightly more likely to be singletons than neutral genes (OR=1.09, p=0.02)
heading: They Are Poorly Characterized Recent Acquisitions

text: Costly+dispensable genes have median length 615 bp versus 765 bp for costly+conserved genes (p=4.2e-75, r=0.170).
quote: - **Shorter**: Median 615 bp vs 765 bp for costly+conserved (p=4.2e-75, rank-biserial r=0.170), consistent with IS elements and gene fragments
heading: They Are Poorly Characterized Recent Acquisitions

text: Figure fig_annotation_rate.png shows SEED and KEGG annotation rates by selection quadrant.
quote: ![Annotation rate (SEED, KEGG) by selection quadrant](figures/fig_annotation_rate.png)
heading: They Are Poorly Characterized Recent Acquisitions

text: Figure fig_ortholog_breadth.png shows ortholog-group breadth and orphan fractions by quadrant.
quote: ![Ortholog group breadth and orphan gene fraction by quadrant](figures/fig_ortholog_breadth.png)
heading: They Are Poorly Characterized Recent Acquisitions

text: Figure fig_gene_length.png shows gene-length distributions by quadrant.
quote: ![Gene length distributions by quadrant](figures/fig_gene_length.png)
heading: They Are Poorly Characterized Recent Acquisitions

text: Fourteen SEED categories, including several core metabolic and cellular functions, are depleted in costly+dispensable genes at FDR < 0.05.
quote: 14 SEED top-level categories are significantly depleted in costly+dispensable genes (FDR < 0.05), including Protein Metabolism, Respiration, Carbohydrates, Amino Acids, Cofactors/Vitamins, Motility, Stress Response, and RNA Metabolism.
heading: Core Metabolism Is Depleted

text: The report interprets costly+conserved genes as costly in lab assays but retained by environmental selection.
quote: These core cellular functions are maintained in the costly+conserved quadrant -- genes whose lab-measured burden is offset by natural selection in the environment.
heading: Core Metabolism Is Depleted

text: Pseudomonas stutzeri RCH2 is the named organism/strain singled out as an outlier.
quote: ### *Pseudomonas stutzeri* RCH2 Is an Outlier
heading: *Pseudomonas stutzeri* RCH2 Is an Outlier

text: Pseudomonas stutzeri RCH2 is an outlier at 21.5% costly+dispensable genes versus 14.0% for the next organism, B. thetaiotaomicron.
quote: psRCH2 contributes 21.5% of its genes as costly+dispensable -- far above the next organism (*B. thetaiotaomicron* at 14.0%).
heading: *Pseudomonas stutzeri* RCH2 Is an Outlier

text: The report proposes a strain-specific recent mobile-element invasion or genomic expansion as a possible explanation for psRCH2.
quote: This suggests a recent mobile element invasion or genomic expansion specific to this strain.
heading: *Pseudomonas stutzeri* RCH2 Is an Outlier

text: Figure fig_organism_distribution.png shows costly+dispensable gene counts by organism.
quote: ![Costly+dispensable gene counts by organism](figures/fig_organism_distribution.png)
heading: *Pseudomonas stutzeri* RCH2 Is an Outlier

text: Figure fig_per_organism.png shows selection-quadrant proportions per organism.
quote: ![Stacked bar of quadrant proportions per organism](figures/fig_per_organism.png)
heading: *Pseudomonas stutzeri* RCH2 Is an Outlier

text: Condition-specific phenotypes occur in 14.1% of costly+dispensable genes, versus 16.7% of costly+conserved and 2.7% of neutral+dispensable genes; the report suggests some costly+dispensable genes can have conditional fitness effects.
quote: Despite being burdensome and non-conserved, 14.1% of costly+dispensable genes have condition-specific phenotypes (vs 16.7% for costly+conserved). This is much higher than neutral+dispensable genes (2.7%), suggesting these genes are not inert -- they can affect fitness under specific conditions, which may slow their loss from the genome.
heading: Costly+Dispensable Genes Still Have Condition-Specific Effects

text: The authors interpret costly+dispensable genes as HGT-associated genomic debris, including insertion sequences, prophage remnants, transposases and defense systems; this is interpretation rather than direct provenance measurement.
quote: The costly+dispensable genes represent the **genomic debris of horizontal gene transfer** -- insertion sequences, prophage remnants, transposases, and defense systems that impose metabolic cost on their host and are not conserved across the species pangenome.
heading: Interpretation

text: The report hypothesizes ongoing loss of costly+dispensable genes unless some environments provide compensating selective advantage.
quote: These genes are candidates for **ongoing gene loss** -- they've been acquired via HGT but impose sufficient cost that they will likely be purged from the genome over evolutionary time unless they provide a selective advantage in specific environments.
heading: Interpretation

text: The comparison group comprises 28,017 costly+conserved genes and is enriched for core-metabolism functions; the evolutionary explanation is interpretive.
quote: The contrast with the 28,017 costly+conserved genes is instructive. Costly+conserved genes are enriched in core metabolism (Protein Metabolism, Respiration, Motility) -- functions that are energetically expensive but maintained by purifying selection because they're essential in natural environments not captured by lab experiments.
heading: Interpretation

text: The Black Queen Hypothesis is the named framework for adaptive loss of costly public-good functions.
quote: - **Morris et al. (2012)** proposed the Black Queen Hypothesis: costly genes can be lost when their functions are provided as public goods by community members.
heading: Literature Context

text: Fitness Browser is a named data source used in the analysis.
quote: - **Price et al. (2018)** generated the Fitness Browser data used here, showing that mutant fitness data can assign phenotypes to genes of unknown function.
heading: Literature Context

text: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a named organism in the cited literature context, not part of the report's direct analysis.
quote: - **Rosconi et al. (2022)** demonstrated that gene essentiality is strain-dependent in *S. pneumoniae*, with the accessory genome modulating which genes are required.
heading: Literature Context

text: The study defines its target genes by improved fitness upon deletion and lack of pangenome conservation.
quote: This is the first systematic characterization of genes that are simultaneously burdensome (fitness improves when deleted) and not conserved in the pangenome.
heading: Novel Contribution

text: The report analyzes 142,190 genes across 43 bacteria.
quote: While mobile element burden has been studied in individual organisms, the cross-organism scale (142,190 genes across 43 bacteria) and the pangenome dimension are new.
heading: Novel Contribution

text: The authors propose HGT-mediated genome expansion rather than metabolic-pathway degradation as the main explanation, but this is interpretive.
quote: The finding that costly+dispensable genes are almost exclusively mobile element debris -- rather than degrading metabolic pathways -- narrows the biological interpretation and suggests that HGT-mediated genome expansion is the primary source of costly non-conserved genes in bacteria.
heading: Novel Contribution

text: The burden criterion is max_fit > 1 in any experiment and is sensitive to single-experiment noise.
quote: - "Burden" is defined as max_fit > 1 in any experiment -- a single experiment can classify a gene as burdensome, making this sensitive to noise in the fitness data
heading: Limitations

text: SEED/KEGG annotations cover only 56-79% of genes; unannotated genes could change functional comparisons.
quote: - SEED/KEGG annotations cover only 56-79% of genes; the unannotated fraction may have different functional profiles
heading: Limitations

text: Binary core/auxiliary classification obscures the fraction of genomes carrying each gene.
quote: - The pangenome core/auxiliary classification is binary; a quantitative measure (fraction of genomes carrying the gene) would provide more resolution
heading: Limitations

text: A 90% identity DIAMOND linking threshold may omit low-similarity acquired genes.
quote: - The 90% identity DIAMOND threshold for FB-pangenome linking may miss recently acquired genes with low sequence similarity
heading: Limitations

text: The 21.5% psRCH2 outlier may be strain-specific and not generalizable.
quote: - psRCH2's extreme outlier status (21.5% costly+dispensable) may reflect strain-specific genomic features rather than a general pattern
heading: Limitations

text: BBH ortholog assignment spans 48 organisms; orthologs outside the set may be missed, inflating orphan calls.
quote: - Ortholog group assignment uses BBH across 48 organisms; genes with orthologs outside this set would be misclassified as orphans
heading: Limitations

text: Condition-specific phenotype evidence is biased toward laboratory-testable conditions.
quote: - Condition-specific phenotype data is biased toward lab-testable conditions
heading: Limitations
